question.text: Some historians believe this tsar lost his sanity when his wife died in 1560. His son Feodor's unsuccessful reign led to the Time of Troubles.
question.clue: He caused a miscarriage in his stepdaughter by beating her, and also killed his son with a blow to the head.

swap.text: After Nicholas abdicated, he and his family were executed, paving the way for this Bolshevik ("BOWL-she-vick") leader to assume power.
swap.clue: A Nikolai Chernyshevsky novel inspired the title of his pamphlet about the importance of forming a vanguard, What Is To Be Done?

question.leadin: He fought in the Great Northern War and created the Table of Ranks.
question.text: This is what Russian czar who cut off the beards of the boyars in an attempt to westernize Russia?
question.answerHtml: Peter the Great [or Peter I; or Pyotr Velikiy; prompt on Peter]
question.clue: He created the table of ranks and required lifetime service from the nobility while defeating Sweden in the Great Northern War.

swap.leadin: This leader may have had her husband, Peter III, killed, so that she could take the throne.
swap.text: Name this 18th century Empress of Russia, an "enlightened despot" who supported the works of Voltaire and Diderot while brutally crushing uprisings like Pugachev's Rebellion.
swap.clue: This ruler backed Stanislaw Poniatowski, then the Targowica Confederation against him, and faced Pugachev's Rebellion.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the beginnings of the Soviet Union.
question.text: This Soviet party was formed counter to Lenin's Bolsheviks in 1904 by Julius Martov. Whereas "Bolshevik" means "majority", this party's name translates as "minority".
question.clue: Jewish-Russian economists associated with the Bund, including (+) Boris Berlatsky, were targeted in one of Stalin's first "Show Trials" named for this political faction.

swap.leadin: The nurse Darya Mikhailova ("mih-HAIL-oh-vuh") took care of Russian soldiers from this war wounded at the Battle of Alma.
swap.text: Name this 1853-1856 war, during which Sevastopol ("seh-VAST-oh-pull") was besieged for eleven months. A group of 38 nurses worked at the Scutari Barracks during this war.
swap.clue: During this conflict, a nurse pioneered the use of pie charts to improve conditions at a hospital at Scutari ("SCOO-tuh-ree").

question.text: This polity under Sviatoslav ("SVYAH-toh-slav") I launched campaigns that largely destroyed Khazar power. This polity's leader Vladimir the Great converted to Christianity and legendarily led a mass baptism.
question.clue: Its leaders used a system of succession in which the throne would pass to the eldest brother of the deceased, called the rota or "ladder" system.

swap.text: Lenin implemented this program in 1921, which allowed for some private ventures, including small businesses operating for profit and some private agriculture. Stalin replaced it with his First Five-Year Plan in 1928.
swap.clue: This policy's namesake "men" often opened casinos and nightclubs.

question.leadin: A traditional folk song of people working on this body of water contains the repeated cry of "Yo, heave ho!"
question.text: Name this body of water. Peasants known as burlaki used harnesses and ropes to drag barges up and down this body of water.
question.clue: Flowing through Nizhniy Novgorod and Samara, this river's canal to the Don provides the most direct connection between the Sea of Azov (AH-soff) and the world's largest lake.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about instances of starvation in history.
swap.text: This horrific 1930s famine wiped out millions in the Ukraine after Stalin's collectivization campaigns pilfered most of the country's crops. It was exacerbated when Moscow outlawed picking food up off the ground and eating it, which was evidently too capitalist.
swap.clue: Possession of food was considered evidence of stealing during this event in which the Red Army isolated an area including Kharkiv and Odessa Oblasts.

question.leadin: This man had a "passion for Western music and scotch."
question.text: Name this man who was KGB Chairman during Prague Spring. As General Secretary, this man succeeded Leonid Brezhnev and continued the war in Afghanistan, but died fifteenth months after taking office.
question.clue: This balding General secretary enjoyed a short-lived tenure as the General Secretary, during which saw the downing of Korean Air Flight KAL-007 and received a letter and a visit from 5th grader Samantha Smith, the "youngest ambassador of the United States". Predictably, his predecessor was the hairy Brezhnev.

swap.text: This man commanded the secret police NKVD until 1946. An ally of Molotov and Georgy Malenkov, he was eventually abandoned by his allies, arrested by Marshal Zhukov's forces, and executed.
swap.clue: With his one-time ally Gregory Malenkov, he eliminated opponents in the Leningrad Affair.

question.leadin: This political party formed in 2001 through a merger of the Fatherland-All Russia and the Unity parties.
question.text: Name this Russian political party that presently controls about 75% of the Duma. It is usually described as a non-ideological "party of power," though its stated ideology is "Russian Conservatism."
question.clue: Nazarbayev is also the chairman of the Nur Otan party, which in 2015 signed a cooperation agreement with this largest political party in Russia, whose incoherent ideology can best be described as "pro-Putin".

swap.text: Although he lost several initial battles at sites like Narva, this Russian leader quickly reorganized his army and proceeded to go on to win at Poltava and the Pruth River.
swap.answer: Peter I or Peter the Great
swap.clue: This ruler tortured a son named Alexei who died in jail.

question.text: This medieval Russian city was home to a quasi-republic where any citizen could call a civic meeting by ringing a bell. It is named similarly to a city sometimes referred to as "Nizhny."
question.answerHtml: Veliky Novgorod [or Novgorod the Great; DO NOT accept or prompt on “Nizhny Novgorod.”]
question.clue: This city's St. Sophia Cathedral is home to the bones of Yaroslav the Wise.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about heroic Soviet urban renaming practices.
swap.text: Volgograd was the site of one of the bloodiest battles in human history, lasting from August 1942 to February 1943, when it was known by this name
swap.clue: In a battle for this city, Operation Uranus resulted in the encirclement of the German Sixth Army under field marshal Friedrich Paulus, which Adolf Hitler then ordered to be supplied from the air.

question.text: The leader of the pro-German government, Pavlo Skoropadskyi, revived the use of this title while leading Ukraine in 1918. This title was traditionally used by leaders of a sich until abolished by Catherine the Great.
question.clue: Holders of this title, who carried a gem-encrusted mace called a bulawa ("boo-WAH-va"), were elected by the Sich ("seetch") Rada.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about anarchist thinkers and their works.
swap.text: Considered to be the founder of Anarchism, this Russian guy escaped from Siberia by going through, Japan, the Panama Canal, and San Francisco before writing Federalism, Socialism and Anti-Theologism and fighting with Marx
swap.clue: This philosopher who outlined his beliefs in works such as Statism and Anarchy. Due to his feuds with Karl Marx, this philosopher was expelled from the International Workingmen's Association in 1872.

question.leadin: Name these things about Alexander Scriabin's uncle, Vyacheslav Scriabin, FTP each.
question.text: As a member of the Politburo Molotov was the key signatory, behind Beria, of the order that caused this execution of 25,000 Poles near the namesake area in 1940.
question.clue: As head of the NKVD, Beria was responsible for masterminding this execution of captive Polish officers in the namesake site in 1940.

swap.text: Though he lost at Borodino, this Russian Field General defended his nation against Napolean's invasion.
swap.clue: He once claimed that he would bury the French at Galicia, but his plan to retreat to the Carpathians was rejected and led to a crushing defeat for his allies.
